structured_output.analysis:
There is only one measured grid so far: iso_3.15, with KL 0.43614 [E514ab09c524e] at 3.14795 average bits. The budget is 84617/26880 ≈ 3.1480 bits, so there is essentially no headroom, and any upgrade has to be paid for with a downgrade. The measured KL is higher than the predicted 0.398, so layers interact more than the per-layer sums suggest.

The loss is concentrated in the MLP layers. For example:
- 27.up_proj: gptq_int3 0.00572 [Ef04d8aa7bded] vs gptq_int4 0.00217 [Efea8c18d2abc]
- 14.down_proj: rht_gptq_int2 0.00633 [E4c3f9b73e065] vs rht_gptq_int3 0.00181 [E90bd4b2f3645]

I don't have per-layer KL for any cheap layer that could fund a downgrade, so I can't build a trustworthy bit-neutral layer swap. This round instead tests changes to method options:
- act_order=true does not change the stored bits.
- A group-size trade gives the int2 layers finer groups (weight.group_size=64) and pays for it with weight.group_size=256 on rht_gptq_int3. Whether that fits the budget depends on assumed per-group scale costs that I haven't measured.

proposals.name: iso_3.15_actorder
proposals.rationale: iso_3.15 measures KL 0.43614 [E514ab09c524e] at 3.14795 bits, which is at the budget. Turning on act_order=true for every GPTQ variant leaves the stored bits unchanged. It targets the losses at 3 bits and below, such as 27.up_proj gptq_int3 0.00572 [Ef04d8aa7bded] and 14.down_proj rht_gptq_int2 0.00633 [E4c3f9b73e065].

proposals.name: iso_3.15_actorder_damp005
proposals.rationale: This keeps the bits of iso_3.15 (KL 0.43614 [E514ab09c524e]) and sets act_order=true with a lower damp=0.005, which fits the Hessian more closely. Most of the loss is in MLP layers at 2 and 3 bits, for example 3.up_proj rht_gptq_int3 0.00642 [E6f4f7ea296d5] and 18.gate_proj rht_gptq_int2 [Eb1dd74cd6447].

proposals.name: iso_3.15_g64int2_g256int3
proposals.rationale: The int2 layers are the most expensive per layer: 14.down_proj rht_gptq_int2 0.00633 vs rht_gptq_int3 0.00181 [E4c3f9b73e065][E90bd4b2f3645], and 11.gate_proj rht_gptq_int2 [E9c454f30c659]. This gives the 28 int2 layers weight.group_size=64. It pays for that by moving the 109 rht_gptq_int3 layers to weight.group_size=256, which halves their scale overhead. The goal is to stay within the 3.148-bit budget of iso_3.15 [E514ab09c524e].
